newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prices drop amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prices drop amid weak demand.

text.p: Light distillate prices fell sharply amid weak demand, unable to find support from cuts in Singapore refinery throughputs, traders said on Monday.
"The light ends aren't really affected by the cuts as refiners have already cut reforming outputs to levels just sufficient to produce hydrogen," said a trader with a European major.
Shell Singapore and Esso Singapore have cut production amid weak margins. SRC said it will cut later this week and Mobil was considering cuts.

A U.S. major denied selling an early February cargo of light naphtha and said he was offering the cargo and an end February/early March cargo at $1.00 per barrel over Singapore quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
But other traders assessed premiums lower at 70-90 cents amid weak demand.
Gasoline was more actively talked with a major heard selling a 95-octane unleaded cargo at $25.50 per barrel lifting February 9-13, fob.
The region had ample supplies with a major in Thailand rumoured to have a February cargo to sell.
A Chinese refiner offered a 93-octane gasoline cargo lifting in second-half February at $1.70 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, fob China.
The only gasoline bid was for 97-octane at $26.70 per barrel
